record: key-provenance exceptions -- committed run_config.json records whose recorded cache_key today's ScenarioConfig.cache_key() cannot recompute
authority: capx D85 (owner ruling Q59, capx ledger §0bb.3(a), r#57) derived every entry below to its exact recorded literal under a named recipe, zero unclassified, and ruled the item BOOKKEEPING, NOT A DEFECT. capx D85-R (§0bc.3(c)) committed the derivation as this checked record. capx D91 (owner ruling Q64, §0bh.3(a)) appended the single `lag` row its own registration repair creates, having counted it before the edit; the count was 1 and so did not change the repair's recommendation.
what_this_is_not: NOT a licence to rewrite a committed cache_key. A committed key is what that bundle actually solved under; rewriting it makes the artifact lie about its own provenance (D85 §5 refuses repair (iv)).
NOT a licence to re-register or un-register a lagging field. Curing the 6 `lag` rows that way orphans every key produced since 2026-09-02 that carries the field (D85 §5 refuses repair (iii)).
NOT a place to park a NEW mismatch. A sixteenth is a FINDING: the lane that meets one stops and reports it, and only an owner card adds a class here.
NOT about the solve-surface re-key. Records that reproduce only with the surface AT DECLARATION are capx D79's designed behaviour, are counted separately by the census, and never appear here.
checked_by: tests/regression/test_key_provenance_exceptions.py (offline; also proves the gate fails on a sixteenth and on a stale entry)

gates.G1_UNKNOWN: a committed record does not reproduce and is not listed here (a SIXTEENTH) -- FAIL
gates.G2_STALE: a listed record now REPRODUCES under HEAD rules -- the entry is dead scaffolding, delete it (rule 26) -- FAIL
gates.G3_RECIPE: a listed record does not reproduce its recorded literal under its own recipe -- FAIL
gates.G4_PRESENT: a listed run_config.json is no longer committed (bundle pruned) -- delete the entry -- FAIL
gates.G5_KEY: a listed recorded_cache_key is not the key the file itself records -- FAIL

recipe_schema.undrop: registered fields kept in the hash even at their drop value (class `lag`)
recipe_schema.roots: [[sentinel, absolute-prefix], ...] replacing the checkout's fold roots (class `split-root`)
recipe_schema.surface: 'declaration' (default) or 'live' -- which of the two cache_key constructions to hash under
recipe_schema.vintage_sha: hash under the rules AST-extracted from that commit's scenarios.py instead of HEAD's
recipe_schema.resolve_iso_overrides: with vintage_sha: first apply that vintage's ISO default_scenario_overrides to the payload

entries.why: Registration lag, and the ONLY record capx D91's repair orphans -- counted and disclosed in that lane's PRECOMMIT BEFORE the edit, not discovered after it. `pjm_seam_neighbour_hourly_ladder` landed in f2a834de (pjm-174) WITHOUT its `_CACHE_KEY_OPTIONAL_FIELDS` entry and was registered 2026-09-09 by capx D91 under owner ruling Q64. This is the one committed payload solved inside that ~33-hour window (2026-09-08T16:21Z -> 2026-09-09T01:57Z), so the solving code HASHED the field at False; today's rule DROPS it at False. Un-dropping that one field reproduces the literal exactly. It is the identical species as the `caiso_offer_surface_measured_ungrounded` lag rows -- same defect, same cure, same class -- and it is not a keeper, not a dashboard-registered run, and not a key-named bundle directory: two JSON files addressed by path. The inverse cost of NOT registering the field was 199 of 200 committed records unable to reconstruct their own key.
entries.citation: docs/handoffs/FINDING-capx-d91-2026-09-09.md §6 (orphan census) and §5 (the registration); owner ruling Q64, capx ledger §0bh.3(a)
